style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph, top-down 90-degree view, on a brushed-steel desk in a dim control room. A printed API rate card in bone-white tactile paper stock lies off-centre on the right third, its faint pricing rows cropped illegible at the frame edge, one row struck through with an oxidised-red pencil rule. Beside it, lower left, the same monthly token bill laid down twice — two identical sheets fanned slightly out of alignment, the December copy doubled. A red pencil rests across the papers. Soft diffused daylight from the left, cool monitor glow rimming the desk edge, muted paper tones, graphite and bone white with oxidised-red accents. 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, generous negative space.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, legible numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: The story's protagonist is a rate notice — the document that changed the economics — and the catalogue reserves document_flatlay for exactly that artefact. A top-down paper still life lets the doubling be shown physically (the same bill, laid down twice) without any legible text, and the handled, pencil-ruled sheet carries the article's own voice of reading the expiry line twice.
cue: One model has a clock on its price
subject: a printed API rate card with one repriced row, beside its monthly token bill laid down twice
core_thesis: Google's own rate card prints Gemini 4 Carbon's price doubling for December 1, but because token bills show spend only by API key or project, most FinOps teams cannot see which of their workloads are standing on the cliff.
core_conflict: A public, dated price schedule on the vendor's rate card versus bills that carry no workload grain — repricing the budget takes an afternoon, but tracing the exposure to workloads does not.
composition: Top-down 90-degree flat-lay, asymmetric: rate card off-centre on the right third, the doubled bill stack lower left, wide graphite negative space above
